Check a task's dispatch records: each needs a Dispatched line with a full SHA, a Model line,
non-empty Checklist and Scope notes sections, a `Package root:` line with an absolute path inside Scope notes, a scope-notes
line naming `main` as the completion recipient, and a checklist that is not only pointer lines (a record name plus only
words from POINTER_WORDS, as in "Same checklist as implementation-2."); a pointer worded outside that set, such as
"Reuse the checklist of implementation-2.", passes.
When the workflow README lists an extension whose EXTENSION.md has an `Instruction FO adds to the scope notes`
bullet, the first record of its `Joins:` stage (`implementation-1.md`) also needs that bullet's script paths with
`<package>` replaced by the record's own `Package root:` value, or a line `<name> not run: <reason>`.

Usage: dispatch_records.py [--readme FILE] <task folder or task .md file>
       dispatch_records.py [--readme FILE] --coverage <task .md file> --stage <worker stage>
       dispatch_records.py --names [--strict] <record file>...
       dispatch_records.py --newest <state checkout> <task slug>
Exit 1 naming each record that lacks a part, or when the task has no dispatch records. The README is FILE, else the
nearest README.md above the task folder with an `entity-type:` line; with neither, the run prints
`extensions not checked: no workflow README above <folder>` and its exit code is unchanged. A missing FILE exits 2.
--names prints `<file>:<line>: bare package script name <NAME>` for each package script (a .py file
directly under <package>/scripts/ or <package>/extensions/<name>/) written with no directory part in the
Checklist or Scope notes section (the whole file when it has neither heading), and exits 1 when any is found.
--names also prints `<file>:1: no 'Candidate: <40-hex head>' line; ...` for a `validation-<N>.md` directly in a `dispatch/` folder
whose text above its first `## ` heading has no line delivery_gate.py accepts; --newest does not.
For a record in `<task folder>/dispatch/` with the task `<task folder>.md` beside the folder, --names also prints
`<file>:1: reserved line 'ADR: NNNN' missing from scope notes; ...` when `implementation-1.md` has no scope-notes line
for each `ADR: NNNN` or `Migration: NNNN` the task's `## Number guards` reserves, and
`<file>:1: Captain amendment N named in no dispatch checklist; ...` when an `### Amendment N` entry of the task's
`## Captain amendments` (fenced lines skipped) is named by no `amendment N` phrase in any `## Checklist` of that folder's records.
`<file>:1: '## FO alignment' records alignment as needed with no 'Result:' line; ...` for an `ideation-<N>.md` whose task has an unfenced
`Alignment: needed` line and no `Result: <text>` line, and `<file>:1: Captain amendment N <Captain|Asked> line holds a backslash-quote copied from JSON; ...`
for a `\"` on a `Captain:` or `Asked:` amendment line outside a `Superseded text:` block.
--names refuses implementation records (including message continuations) for Pilot/Prod when the last unfenced
`## Design` (also ` — title` or `: title`) contains `docs/adr/<placeholder>-title.md` and task_facts has no reserved ADR.
Quoted/fenced paths and numbered citations do not signal this obligation; scope-copy checks stay first-record-only.
A record whose task file is absent is not judged by task-fact checks.
--names reports skipped context checks on stderr. --strict requires --names and at least one record;
it exits 2 for a record outside task/dispatch or without an adjacent task file, after running the existing checks.
--names also refuses a live validation rerun with open F-numbered Needs decision findings until a later
committed native Captain validation resolution or Captain amendment exists (ADR 0045). It skips this predicate
for non-git snapshots; missing or ambiguous required git history exits 2.
--newest runs that scan on the file added by the latest commit that adds a file under <slug>/dispatch/, read as it
is on disk: exit 0 when it is clean or the task has no record, 1 when a name is found, 2 when git cannot read the state.
--coverage checks presence for a declared ideation, implementation or validation stage after an unfenced report:
exit 0 when not due or covered, 1 when missing, 2 for invalid input or read errors. A positive-numbered stage
record or stage message record covers repeated reports; contents and historical send timing are not checked.
